A self-guided Totterdown walk

Updated 2 November 2026. Totterdown is very steep, so wear good shoes and take your time. Most stops are on residential streets: keep noise down and don't block doors. How we check facts.

These ten sights run roughly from the river at the bottom of the hill to the top, so you can link them into a walk from Temple Meads station. Each has a map link to help you plan your own route.

Quick answer

  • Start: Bristol Temple Meads, at the foot of the hill. [1]
  • Highlights: the Three Lamps signpost, the coloured terraces and Vale Street, England's steepest residential street. [2] [3] [4]
  • Finish: the view from Perrett's Park, or a drink on the Wells Road on the way back down. [5] [6]
  • Ready-made routes: Visit Bristol, TRESA and the Friends of the Avon New Cut all publish walks that pass through or near Totterdown. [1] [7] [8]

The ten sights

  1. Bristol Temple Meads. The station is the natural starting point; Visit Bristol's walk from here crosses the New Cut and climbs into Totterdown. [1] Map
  2. Totterdown Bridge. The bridge over the Avon at the foot of the hill was built in 1888. [9] Map
  3. The Thunderbolt, 124 Bath Road. A Grade II listed turnpike tollhouse from about 1840, now a music pub. [10] Map
  4. Three Lamps. The Grade II* listed cast-iron signpost where the Bath Road and the Wells Road part, its arms pointing to Bath and Wells. [2] Map
  5. The lost middle of Totterdown. Around Three Lamps stood the streets cleared from about 1968 for a road that was never built. [11] [12] The full story.
  6. Bristol Jamia Mosque, Green Street. Bristol's first mosque, in a former church bought in 1968. [13] Map
  7. Richmond Street. One of the best-known rows of coloured houses, with more than 70 homes, most of them brightly painted. [3] Map
  8. Vale Street. England's steepest residential street, home to the Easter egg roll, and briefly to Banksy's "Aachoo!!". [4] [14] Vale Street guide. Map
  9. The Wells Road. Totterdown's high street, with cafés, pizza and the Bruhaha brewpub. [6] [15] Where to eat. Map
  10. Perrett's Park. Finish with one of the best views of the city, especially at Balloon Fiesta time in August. [5] Map

How can you extend the walk?

  • Arnos Vale Cemetery: a Victorian garden cemetery further along the Bath Road. [16] More.
  • Religious buildings: TRESA's walk visits Totterdown's churches, chapels and mosque. [7]
  • The river: the Friends of the Avon New Cut publish circular walks along the New Cut. [8]
  • On the arts trail weekend you can go inside artists' homes along the way: 14 and 15 November in 2026. [17] Arts trail guide.
